title: Lead RRP cleaning verification and dust clearance practice questions
description: Free Lead RRP practice questions on cleaning verification and optional dust clearance testing, 40 CFR 745.85(b)-(c). Every answer quotes the rule.

questions.topic: Key terms and who performs verification
questions.question: Under 745.90(b)(1), who must perform the post-renovation cleaning verification tasks described in 745.85(b)?

options.A: A worker trained on the job and directed by the certified renovator
options.B: The firm employee who prepares the project records
options.C: A certified renovator
options.D: The building owner or an adult occupant

questions.explanation: A certified renovator "Must perform all of the tasks described in § 745.85(b) and must either perform or direct workers who perform all of the tasks described in § 745.85(a)." Directing workers is allowed only for the 745.85(a) tasks.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Must perform all of the tasks described in § 745.85(b) and must either perform or direct workers who perform all of the tasks described in § 745.85(a).

questions.topic: Key terms and who performs verification
questions.question: According to the definition in 745.83, what is a cleaning verification card used to determine?

options.A: Whether post-renovation cleaning has been properly completed, by comparing wet and dry disposable cleaning cloths with the card
options.B: Whether paint contains lead at or above 1.0 milligrams per square centimeter
options.C: Whether a dust-lead hazard is present under 745.65(b)
options.D: The amount of lead in a dust sample, in micrograms per square foot

questions.explanation: The card is "for the purpose of determining, through comparison of wet and dry disposable cleaning cloths with the card, whether post-renovation cleaning has been properly completed."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.83, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Cleaning verification card means a card developed and distributed, or otherwise approved, by EPA for the purpose of determining, through comparison of wet and dry disposable cleaning cloths with the card, whether post-renovation cleaning has been properly completed.

questions.question: During interior cleaning verification, the certified renovator's visual inspection finds dust still present. What does 745.85(b)(1)(i) require next?

options.A: Wipe the windowsills with a dry disposable cleaning cloth
options.B: Have a certified risk assessor collect dust samples
options.C: Remove the warning signs and note the dust in the records
options.D: Remove the dust by re-cleaning and perform another visual inspection

questions.explanation: "If dust, debris or residue is present, these conditions must be removed by re-cleaning and another visual inspection must be performed."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: If dust, debris or residue is present, these conditions must be removed by re-cleaning and another visual inspection must be performed.

questions.question: For an interior renovation, at what point does 745.85(b)(1)(iii) direct that the warning signs be removed?

options.A: As soon as the protective sheeting has been removed
options.B: When the work area passes the post-renovation cleaning verification
options.C: When the renovation work itself is finished, before any cleaning
options.D: When the firm delivers the final invoice

questions.explanation: "When the work area passes the post-renovation cleaning verification, remove the warning signs." Under 745.85(a)(1) the signs "must remain in place and readable until the renovation and the post-renovation cleaning verification have been completed."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: When the work area passes the post-renovation cleaning verification, remove the warning signs.

questions.question: What does 745.85(b)(2) require a certified renovator to do to verify cleaning after an exterior renovation?

options.A: Perform a visual inspection for dust, debris or residue on surfaces in and below the work area, including windowsills and the ground
options.B: Wipe the ground below the work area with wet disposable cleaning cloths and compare them with the card
options.C: Wipe each exterior windowsill with a wet cloth and compare it with the card
options.D: Divide the ground covering into sections of less than 40 square feet and wipe each one

questions.explanation: "A certified renovator must perform a visual inspection to determine whether dust, debris or residue is still present on surfaces in and below the work area, including windowsills and the ground."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A certified renovator must perform a visual inspection to determine whether dust, debris or residue is still present on surfaces in and below the work area, including windowsills and the ground.

questions.question: A painter returns after post-renovation cleaning verification has been performed to apply paint to walls that were already prepared. How does 745.85(d) treat this work?

options.A: It must be directed by a certified renovator who is on site
options.B: It requires a new round of cleaning verification
options.C: It is not regulated by Subpart E, because it does not disturb paint and comes after cleaning verification
options.D: It requires the warning signs to be posted again

questions.explanation: "Activities that do not disturb paint, such as applying paint to walls that have already been prepared, are not regulated by this subpart if they are conducted after post-renovation cleaning verification has been performed."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Activities that do not disturb paint, such as applying paint to walls that have already been prepared, are not regulated by this subpart if they are conducted after post-renovation cleaning verification has been performed.

questions.question: An interior windowsill has been re-cleaned and wiped again, and the cloth still does not match and is darker than the cleaning verification card. What waiting period does 745.85(b)(1)(ii)(A)(3) set?

options.A: 30 minutes, then wipe again with a new wet cloth
options.B: 1 hour or until the surface has dried completely, whichever is longer
options.C: 24 hours, then re-clean the windowsill a third time
options.D: No waiting period; wipe again at once with a dry cloth

questions.explanation: "If the cloth does not match and is darker than the cleaning verification card, wait for 1 hour or until the surface has dried completely, whichever is longer."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the cloth does not match and is darker than the cleaning verification card, wait for 1 hour or until the surface has dried completely, whichever is longer.

questions.question: After re-cleaning a windowsill whose first cloth was darker than the card, which cloth does 745.85(b)(1)(ii)(A)(2) allow for the next wipe?

options.A: Only a dry disposable cleaning cloth
options.B: Only the same side of the cloth used for the first wipe
options.C: Only a cloth rinsed in clean water
options.D: Either a new cloth or the used cloth folded so that an unused surface is exposed

questions.explanation: After re-cleaning, "either use a new cloth or fold the used cloth in such a way that an unused surface is exposed, and wipe the surface again."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: then either use a new cloth or fold the used cloth in such a way that an unused surface is exposed, and wipe the surface again.

questions.question: How does 745.85(b)(1)(ii)(B) require uncarpeted floors to be wiped for cleaning verification?

options.A: By hand, with the cloth folded in quarters
options.B: With a HEPA vacuum equipped with a beater bar
options.C: With a 2-bucket mopping method that keeps wash water separate from rinse water
options.D: Using an application device with a long handle and a head to which the cloth is attached

questions.explanation: "Floors must be wiped using an application device with a long handle and a head to which the cloth is attached." HEPA vacuuming and the 2-bucket method are cleaning steps in 745.85(a)(5)(ii), not the verification wipe.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Floors must be wiped using an application device with a long handle and a head to which the cloth is attached.

questions.question: The uncarpeted floor within an interior work area is greater than 40 square feet. What does 745.85(b)(1)(ii)(B) require?

options.A: Divide it into roughly equal sections that are each less than 40 square feet and wipe each section separately with a new wet disposable cleaning cloth
options.B: Wipe one representative section of 40 square feet and treat the result as covering the whole floor
options.C: Wipe the whole floor with one wet cloth, refolding it as needed
options.D: Collect a dust wipe sample from the floor for laboratory analysis instead of using the card

questions.explanation: The surface "must be divided into roughly equal sections that are each less than 40 square feet. Wipe each such section separately with a new wet disposable cleaning cloth."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: the surface within the work area must be divided into roughly equal sections that are each less than 40 square feet. Wipe each such section separately with a new wet disposable cleaning cloth.

questions.question: After the waiting period for a floor that did not pass, which sections does 745.85(b)(1)(ii)(B)(3) say to wipe with a dry disposable cleaning cloth?

options.A: Every section in the work area, including those that already passed
options.B: Only sections larger than 40 square feet
options.C: Each section of the surface that has not yet achieved post-renovation cleaning verification
options.D: Only the first section that failed

questions.explanation: "After waiting for the entire surface within the work area to dry, wipe each section of the surface that has not yet achieved post-renovation cleaning verification with a dry disposable cleaning cloth."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: wipe each section of the surface that has not yet achieved post-renovation cleaning verification with a dry disposable cleaning cloth.

questions.question: Under 745.85(c), cleaning verification need not be performed if dust clearance sampling (meeting the conditions listed there) is required by what?

options.A: The certified renovator's own decision on site
options.B: The contract between the renovation firm and the person contracting for the renovation, or another Federal, State, Territorial, Tribal, or local law or regulation
options.C: A verbal request from an occupant during the job
options.D: A note in the firm's own written safety plan

questions.explanation: "Cleaning verification need not be performed if the contract between the renovation firm and the person contracting for the renovation or another Federal, State, Territorial, Tribal, or local law or regulation requires" the items in (c)(1) to (3).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.85(c)(2), who is required to collect the dust clearance samples?

options.A: A certified inspector, risk assessor or dust sampling technician
options.B: The certified renovator assigned to the project
options.C: Any worker trained by the certified renovator
options.D: The building owner, using a recognized test kit

questions.explanation: "The dust clearance samples are required to be collected by a certified inspector, risk assessor or dust sampling technician."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The dust clearance samples are required to be collected by a certified inspector, risk assessor or dust sampling technician.

questions.question: Under 745.85(c)(3), until what result is the renovation firm required to re-clean the work area?

options.A: Until a wet disposable cleaning cloth matches the cleaning verification card
options.B: Until no reportable level of lead is found in any sample
options.C: Until the occupant signs off on the cleaning
options.D: Until the dust sample results are below the dust-lead action levels in 745.227(e)(8) or any applicable State, Territorial, Tribal, or local standard

questions.explanation: The firm must "re-clean the work area until the dust sample results are below the dust-lead action levels in § 745.227(e)(8) or any applicable State, Territorial, Tribal, or local standard."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.85, Work practice standards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The renovation firm is required to re-clean the work area until the dust sample results are below the dust-lead action levels in § 745.227(e)(8) or any applicable State, Territorial, Tribal, or local standard.

questions.question: Under 745.90(a)(3), which individuals may act as certified dust sampling technicians without further training?

options.A: Certified renovators
options.B: Individuals who completed an accredited abatement worker course
options.C: Individuals currently certified as lead-based paint inspectors or risk assessors
options.D: Workers trained on the job by a certified renovator

questions.explanation: "Individuals who are currently certified as lead-based paint inspectors or risk assessors may act as certified dust sampling technicians without further training."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Individuals who are currently certified as lead-based paint inspectors or risk assessors may act as certified dust sampling technicians without further training.

questions.question: When performing optional dust clearance sampling, what does 745.90(c)(1) require a certified dust sampling technician to do with the collected samples?

options.A: Compare the wipes with the cleaning verification card on site
options.B: Send them to a laboratory recognized by EPA under TSCA section 405(b) and compare the results to the action levels in accordance with 745.227(e)(8)
options.C: Give them to the certified renovator, who compares the results
options.D: Keep them on file with the firm's records without analysis

questions.explanation: The technician "must send the collected samples to a laboratory recognized by EPA under TSCA section 405(b), and must compare the results to the action levels in accordance with § 745.227(e)(8)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must send the collected samples to a laboratory recognized by EPA under TSCA section 405(b), and must compare the results to the action levels in accordance with § 745.227(e)(8).

questions.question: What action level does 745.227(e)(8)(viii) set for lead in dust on interior window sills on or after January 12, 2026?

options.A: 250 µg/ft2
options.B: 40 µg/ft2
options.C: 400 µg/ft2
options.D: 5 µg/ft2

questions.explanation: "On or after January 12, 2026, the action levels for lead in dust are 5 µg/ft2 for floors, 40 µg/ft2 for interior window sills, and 100 µg/ft2 for window troughs."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.227, Work practice standards for conducting lead-based paint activities: target housing and child-occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: On or after January 12, 2026, the action levels for lead in dust are 5 µg/ft2 for floors, 40 µg/ft2 for interior window sills, and 100 µg/ft2 for window troughs.

questions.question: According to 745.61(d), what are the levels identified in 745.227(e)(8)(viii) referred to as on or after January 13, 2025?

options.A: Dust-lead hazard standards
options.B: Reportable levels
options.C: Cleaning verification levels
options.D: Action levels

questions.explanation: "Before January 13, 2025, the levels identified in 40 CFR 745.227(e)(8)(viii) were referred to as clearance levels. On or after January 13, 2025, the levels identified in § 745.227(e)(8)(viii) are referred to as action levels."

questions.question: In the certified renovator's certification under 745.86(b)(6)(viii), what must the brief description of the cleaning verification results include?

options.A: The number of wet and dry cloths used
options.B: The name of the laboratory that analyzed the cloths
options.C: Photographs of each cloth next to the card
options.D: The dust-lead results in micrograms per square foot

questions.explanation: The certification states that "The certified renovator performed the post-renovation cleaning verification (the results of which must be briefly described, including the number of wet and dry cloths used)."

questions.evidence: The certified renovator performed the post-renovation cleaning verification (the results of which must be briefly described, including the number of wet and dry cloths used).

questions.question: A pipe bursts and a firm performs an emergency renovation as defined in 745.82(b). How does that paragraph treat the cleaning verification requirements of 745.85(b)?

options.A: They are waived to the extent necessary to respond to the emergency
options.B: They may be performed by any worker trained under 745.90(b)(2)
options.C: They are not exempt and must be performed by certified renovators
options.D: They are replaced by a visual check by the building owner

questions.explanation: "Emergency renovations are not exempt from" the cleaning requirements, "the cleaning verification requirements of § 745.85(b), which must be performed by certified renovators," and certain recordkeeping requirements.
